paper.title: Structure-based out-of-distribution (OOD) materials property prediction: a benchmark study
paper.research_summary: This paper presents a comprehensive benchmark study evaluating graph neural network (GNN) models for predicting material properties on out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets—materials structurally or property-wise distinct from the training set. It introduces five OOD test set generation methods (LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseXcluster, SparseYsingle, SparseYcluster) applied to three MatBench datasets (dielectric, elasticity, perovskites), trains and evaluates eight SOTA GNNs across 250 folds, and analyzes performance degradation relative to i.i.d. baselines, revealing significant generalization gaps and identifying CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DeeperGATGNN as comparatively robust.

tasks.objective: To objectively evaluate ML model performances in property prediction of out-of-distribution (OOD) materials that are different from the training set
constraints: test set comprises no labeled samples
OOD test sets must deviate significantly from training/validation set in distribution
evaluation must reflect real-world material discovery where outlier materials are of interest
output_goal: predicted property values for OOD materials
quantified generalization gap (e.g., MAE increase over i.i.d. baseline)

evidence.text: It is thus a pressing question to provide an objective evaluation of ML model performances in property prediction of out-of-distribution (OOD) materials that are different from the training set.
Here we present a comprehensive benchmark study of structure-based graph neural networks (GNNs) for extrapolative OOD materials property prediction.
We formulated five different categories of OOD ML problems for three benchmark datasets from the MatBench study.

stages.stage_name_raw: Preprocessing crystal structures into OFM feature space and applying t-SNE
stages.stage_goal: Convert raw crystal structures into low-dimensional representations for clustering-based OOD test set generation

evidence.text: Initially, we apply the k-means algorithm61 based on the orbital-field matrix (OFM) features62 to cluster the whole dataset into 50 clusters. OFM captures the electronic structure of materials by considering the orbitals’ interactions, which are fundamental to understanding the material’s properties, and easily interpretable due to their physical basis63. The OFM features were calculated fast using the MatMiner23 package.

In this method, we begin by converting material structures into the 1024-dimension OFM feature space. Subsequently, we apply the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)64 for dimension reduction converting the OFM feature space to a 2D space (x-value).

stages.stage_name_raw: Generating five types of OOD test sets via clustering and density estimation
stages.stage_goal: Produce five distinct OOD test set configurations (LOCO, SparseXsingle, SparseXcluster, SparseYsingle, SparseYcluster) that deviate from training distribution

evidence.text: We proposed five practical scenarios for predicting material properties. These scenarios are designed to focus on properties of less common or underrepresented materials in the dataset, which are often of particular interest to material researchers who are more interested in discovering novel exceptional outlier materials.

We propose the following target set generation methods to simulate real-world conditions for materials property prediction.
Leave-one-cluster-out (LOCO). [...] Single-point targets with the lowest structure density (SparseXsingle). [...] Single-point targets with the lowest property density (SparseYsingle). [...] Cluster targets with the lowest structure density (SparseXcluster). [...] Cluster targets with the lowest property density (SparseYcluster).

stages.stage_name_raw: Training eight GNN models on each fold using OOD train/val splits
stages.stage_goal: Train each GNN model on the training+validation portion of each 50-fold OOD split
stage_input: GNN architectures (CGCNN, SchNet, MEGNet, DimeNet++, ALIGNN, DeeperGATGNN, coGN, coNGN)

evidence.text: For each fold, we selected a cluster as the test set, and the rest as training and validation sets, and averaged the results over 50 folds to get the final result.
In total, we trained a total of 6000 deep learning GNN models, analyzed the results and drew important conclusions from them.

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluating model performance using MAE on OOD test sets
stages.stage_goal: Quantify prediction accuracy of each trained GNN on its corresponding OOD test fold using mean absolute error (MAE)
stage_output: aggregated MAE per model per OOD type

evidence.text: We use the mean absolute error (MAE) metric, which is a standard evaluation criterion for regression-based materials property prediction problems.
